item.title: Suspicious mailings to election officials, congressional offices under investigation
item.description: The FBI and U.S. Postal Inspection Service are looking into the mailings, some of which included an unidentified powdery white substance.

item.title: U.S. historic preservation law faces the most serious threat in its 60-year history
item.description: Congress and a federal agency are threatening to weaken the country's historic preservation law, fueling a backlash that critics say is as fiery as the one that led to the law's creation 60 years ago.

item.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space
item.description: The Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel says Musk and Bezos each want to colonize the moon, mine its resources and launch thousands more satellites. He says their only real competition is each other.

item.title: After booting 760K off ACA health plans, the Trump administration adds some people back
item.description: The Trump administration provided few details about its process for canceling hundreds of thousands of Affordable Care Act enrollments — even as the next stage of the anti-fraud effort is underway.

item.title: These swing voters regret voting for Trump and it's influencing their midterm choices
item.description: Some key voters in Georgia say deep frustration and disappointment with President Trump are motivating their election plans just weeks before Election Day.

item.title: Trump cancels public execution, but a line may already have been crossed
item.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth's announcement of a livestreamed execution elicited reactions of disgust and condemnation from some faith leaders and politicians. But within his church, it's not an outlier.

item.title: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns following misconduct allegations
item.description: President Trump has forced out his ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle. She faced allegations of misconduct before and during her tenure at the U.S. Embassy in Athens, which she has denied.

item.title: Civil rights advocates plan to send thousands of observers to midterm polling places
item.description: For many election cycles, civil rights groups and political parties have fanned out to monitor polling places, but the charged midterm environment has many organizations stepping up efforts this year.

item.title: In Kansas, a newly competitive Senate race tests limit of Trump's unpopular policies
item.description: Kansas voters could send a Democrat to the Senate for the first time in nearly a century — and flip the governor's office back to Republican control, even in what could be a tough year for the GOP.
